suspended_reason: The cause is a MITOCHONDRIAL-GENOME (mtDNA) POINT MUTATION -- most commonly m.11778G>A in MT-ND4 (~60-80% worldwide), with m.3460G>A (MT-ND1) and m.14484T>C (MT-ND6) making up most of the remainder -- in genes of respiratory-chain Complex I, NOT a single-gene NUCLEAR promoter switch. Three features place it outside the kit's read. (1) The lesion is in the ~16.6-kb circular MITOCHONDRIAL genome, which is transcribed as long POLYCISTRONIC transcripts from the mitochondrial heavy/light-strand promoters and then processed -- there is NO nuclear-style TSS-2000..+500 promoter window for MT-ND4 from which to read a gamma switch (the kit's data path resolves NUCLEAR RefSeq promoters; mtDNA protein genes have no such promoter). (2) Penetrance is HETEROPLASMY-dependent and incomplete -- only a minority of carriers of a primary mutation ever lose vision (markedly more often male than female, with partial spontaneous recovery in a subset, plus nuclear-background, mitochondrial-haplogroup and environmental modifiers) -- a continuous, tissue-variable quantity a strand-symmetric single-promoter switch cannot capture. (3) Inheritance is MATERNAL (mitochondrial), not Mendelian. Held per the author's rule (no analyzable single-gene NUCLEAR promoter DNA -> hold). This is a FIFTH held mechanism class -- distinct from WHOLE-CHROMOSOME ANEUPLOIDY (Down), parent-of-origin IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman 15q11-q13; Beckwith-Wiedemann 11p15.5), and REPEAT-CONTRACTION / CHROMATIN-DEREPRESSION (FSHD D4Z4 / DUX4) -- proving the suspension rule keys on the LESION MECHANISM and now generalises to the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME. SHARPEST DISCIPLINE POINT: LHON is suspended DESPITE having an APPROVED drug -- idebenone (Raxone), a coenzyme-Q10 analogue approved for LHON in the EU, Israel, South Korea and elsewhere (US FDA priority review pending as of early 2026) -- and active gene-therapy programmes (intravitreal allotopically expressed MT-ND4, e.g. lenadogene nolparvovec). Idebenone acts DOWNSTREAM (antioxidant / electron-carrier support of retinal ganglion cells) and does not address the mtDNA lesion. The suspension therefore keys purely on whether the ENGINE can READ the lesion (an mtDNA point mutation with no nuclear promoter window, plus heteroplasmy), NOT on whether a therapy exists -- the discipline is about engine-readability, not therapeutic availability. (This is the inverse of the Huntington/XLRP/choroideremia pattern, where the DNA is readable but the lead therapy is unproven: here a therapy is approved but the DNA is unreadable by a nuclear-promoter engine.) An mtDNA / heteroplasmy / Complex-I model is future work, not a single-(nuclear)-switch emergence.
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
